steps.title: Import Vue and required composition APIs (ref, computed)
steps.instruction: Import Vue, ref, and computed from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules for reactive state management.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing Vue composition APIs
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue, ref, and computed from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue package and its composition APIs are imported, enabling reactive state and computed properties.
successCriteria: Vue, ref, and computed are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue, ref, and computed. These are essential for building reactive components with the Composition API.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import all three: Vue, ref, and computed from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is incorrect or incomplete. Check that you're importing Vue, ref, and computed from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the usePermissions composition function
steps.instruction: Define and export a function named usePermissions that accepts a user object parameter.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes a user parameter. Use the function keyword or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue, ref, and computed from 'vue'

// Define and export the usePermissions function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A usePermissions function is defined and exported, ready to accept a user object.
successCriteria: The usePermissions function is defined and exported, and it accepts a user parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the usePermissions composition function. This will serve as the foundation for our RBAC permission logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the function is named exactly 'usePermissions' and accepts a user parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Create a function named usePermissions that takes a user parameter.

steps.title: Initialize reactive user permissions state
steps.instruction: Inside the usePermissions function, create a reactive userPermissions variable using ref with the user.permissions value
steps.hint: Use the ref function to create a reactive reference. Pass the user.permissions value as the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating reactive state with ref
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePermissions function will have a reactive userPermissions state initialized with the user's permissions.
successCriteria: userPermissions is declared using ref with user.permissions as the initial value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive state for user permissions using ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref to create the reactive state and passing user.permissions as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside usePermissions, create a userPermissions variable using ref(user.permissions).

steps.title: Create computed property for admin permission check
steps.instruction: Inside the usePermissions function, create a computed property called isAdmin that returns true if the userPermissions array includes the string 'admin'.
steps.hint: Use the computed function imported from Vue. It takes a getter function that returns a boolean based on whether userPermissions includes 'admin'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The isAdmin computed property will reactively track whether the user has admin permissions.
successCriteria: The usePermissions function contains a computed property named isAdmin that checks if userPermissions includes 'admin'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a computed property that will reactively track admin permissions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using computed() and checking if userPermissions includes 'admin'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property isn't set up correctly. Remember to use computed() and check if userPermissions includes 'admin'.

steps.title: Create computed property for editor permission check
steps.instruction: Inside the usePermissions function, create a computed property called isEditor that returns true if userPermissions includes the string 'editor'.
steps.hint: Use the computed function from Vue to create a reactive property that checks if 'editor' exists in the userPermissions array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePermissions function will have a computed property isEditor that returns a boolean based on whether 'editor' is in userPermissions.
successCriteria: The isEditor computed property is defined inside usePermissions and correctly checks if userPermissions includes 'editor'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the isEditor computed property for checking editor permissions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure isEditor is a computed property that checks if 'editor' exists in userPermissions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isEditor computed property is missing or incorrectly implemented. It should return true when userPermissions includes 'editor'.

steps.title: Create computed property for viewer permission check
steps.instruction: Inside the usePermissions function, create a computed property called isViewer that returns true if userPermissions includes the string 'viewer'.
steps.hint: Use computed() to create a reactive property that checks if 'viewer' exists in the userPermissions array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePermissions function will now have a computed property isViewer that correctly checks for viewer permissions.
successCriteria: A computed property named isViewer is defined and returns true when userPermissions includes 'viewer'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the isViewer computed property to check for viewer permissions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure isViewer is defined as a computed property that checks if 'viewer' exists in userPermissions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isViewer computed property is missing or incorrect. It should be a computed property that returns true when userPermissions includes 'viewer'.

steps.title: Return the permission check functions from the hook
steps.instruction: Return an object from the usePermissions function containing the three computed properties: isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer.
steps.hint: At the end of your function, use the return statement with an object that includes your computed properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePermissions function will now expose the three permission check functions for use in components.
successCriteria: The usePermissions function returns an object containing isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer computed properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the permission check functions from your hook, making them available to any component that uses it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object with all three computed properties: isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The usePermissions function should return an object containing the three computed permission check functions.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create and export a default Vue component named App with a setup() function that returns an empty template.
steps.hint: Define a new component function called App. Use the setup() composition API function and return an empty render function or template.
steps.expectedOutcome: A default exported App component with a setup() function is created, ready to be filled with permission logic and UI.
successCriteria: App component is defined with setup() and exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure. Next we'll add the permission hook and UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named App with a setup() function and exported it as default.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a component with setup() and exported it correctly.

steps.title: Define sample user data in the App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's setup function, create a user object with a permissions property set to ['viewer', 'editor'].
steps.hint: Define a constant user variable with the required structure. This will be passed to the usePermissions hook later.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now contains a user object with the specified permissions array, ready to be used with the permission hook.
successCriteria: A user constant is defined inside setup() with a permissions property containing ['viewer', 'editor'].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the sample user data that will be used to test the permission hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the user object has a permissions property with exactly ['viewer', 'editor'].
steps.feedbackWrong: The user object should be defined inside setup() with permissions: ['viewer', 'editor'].

steps.title: Use the permission hook in the App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's setup function, call the usePermissions hook with the user object and destructure the returned isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer computed properties.
steps.hint: Call the hook with the user object you defined earlier, then destructure the three computed properties from the returned object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: calling a custom hook and destructuring
const { isLoggedIn, canEdit } = useAuth(currentUser);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have access to the three permission computed properties (isAdmin, isEditor, isViewer) from the usePermissions hook.
successCriteria: The usePermissions hook is called with the user object, and isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer are destructured from the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the usePermissions hook and destructured the permission computed properties. Now the component has access to these reactive permission checks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling usePermissions with the user object and destructuring all three computed properties (isAdmin, isEditor, isViewer).
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook needs to be called with the user object, and the three computed properties need to be destructured from the returned object.

steps.title: Create the template structure with permission displays
steps.instruction: In the App component's return object, add a template property that returns three div elements to display the isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer values.
steps.hint: The template should be a string containing HTML with Vue template syntax to display the computed values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a template property that will display the three permission states when rendered.
successCriteria: The App component's return object includes a template property with three div elements displaying isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer values using Vue template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the template structure to display the permission states.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template includes all three div elements with the correct Vue syntax to display isAdmin, isEditor, and isViewer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Check that you've added a template property to the return object with three div elements showing the permission values.

steps.title: Add descriptive labels to the permission displays
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, add descriptive text labels before each permission value display. Add 'Admin Access:' before the admin display, 'Editor Access:' before the editor display, and 'Viewer Access:' before the viewer display.
steps.hint: Add text labels directly in the template before the existing permission value displays. You can use plain text or wrap them in <span> elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show clear labels before each permission status, making it more user-friendly and understandable.
successCriteria: The template contains descriptive text labels 'Admin Access:', 'Editor Access:', and 'Viewer Access:' displayed before their respective permission values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added descriptive labels to make the permission displays clearer and more user-friendly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some labels, but make sure all three permission displays have their descriptive labels: 'Admin Access:', 'Editor Access:', and 'Viewer Access:'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The permission displays don't have the required descriptive labels. Add text labels 'Admin Access:', 'Editor Access:', and 'Viewer Access:' before each permission value display.
